claim: The 1M-fund licence scale is withdrawn, but the replacement test is not evaluable: 'reachable by named target sponsors' presupposes a named list that does not exist, and report 05 itself concludes break-even needs about 100k funds across 10-20 sponsors 'when only 20 such sponsors exist'. The base case ($91 at 100k funds) is therefore still an unsupported scale.
evidence: requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/data/convergence-clauses.jsonl CNV-ECO-003: 'The licence used in any comparison SHALL be computed at the platform scale reachable by named target sponsors within five years, never above the addressable market.' CNV-ECO-004: 'A target sponsor list ... SHALL be maintained' (no list in repo). requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/05-ECONOMIC-VALIDATION.md EV-01: 'roughly $80-130 per fund at 50-100k platform funds, i.e. 10-20 sponsors of 5,000 funds when only 20 such sponsors exist'.
recommended_change: Define platform scale as the sum over the maintained target list of (funds x stage-gated adoption probability); base, favourable and adverse licence prices SHALL be computed at that scale; any run needing more than a stated share of listed sponsors is labelled share-dependent with the share shown. AC: a model run whose scale exceeds the target-list sum, or whose licence is below the P90 break-even at that scale, cannot be headlined.

claim: A vendor P&L is now required, but the viability test is contribution margin, which is the measure the finding said excludes the costs that matter (sales, implementation, build capex, compliance staff, assurance). A configuration can pass 'positive contribution margin' while Unbound loses money; whose margin (sponsor, administrator or Unbound) is also unstated.
evidence: requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/data/convergence-clauses.jsonl CNV-ECO-003: 'Unbound SHALL maintain a vendor P&L (revenue ramp by segment, sales and implementation per sponsor, build and maintenance capex, compliance staff, assurance fees) and a configuration SHALL be called viable only if contribution margin is positive at P90 cost and adverse licence scale.' requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/05-ECONOMIC-VALIDATION.md section 2: break-even licence $81/fund at 100k funds 'including build amortisation and sales'.
recommended_change: Replace the viability test with: vendor fully-loaded annual result (including amortised capex, sales, implementation, compliance staff, assurance fees) is non-negative at P90 cost and adverse licence scale at the target-list scale, and name the party whose margin is tested. AC: a configuration with positive contribution margin but negative fully-loaded result is reported 'not viable'.

claim: The charity-signed-letter-alone loophole is closed and an NOC exemption added, but the minimum evidence combination is ambiguous, cooling-off is only incorporated by reference, and three of the finding's acceptance tests are missing: (a) 'bank-originated match' alone vs 'callback continues to apply'; (b) no lower bound or AC for cooling-off; (c) no per-sponsor scoping of destination evidence; (d) the callback contact is sourced from a 'registry' that has no provenance rule (see new defects).

recommended_change: State the evidence table once: (a) owner match plus cooling-off plus both-channel notice; (b) document plus registry-sourced callback plus cooling-off plus notice. Cooling-off default 3 business days, sponsor may lengthen, never below 1. Destination evidence scoped per sponsor; cross-sponsor reuse only under a written reliance policy. ACs: release before day 3 refused; both previous and new channels notified; sponsor B does not inherit sponsor A's verification.

SHALL leave the sponsor able to pay through its own bank channel'; AC 'the freeze expires or converts'. Finding ADV-T-002 AC: 'queued instruction for G is never dispatched' after OutOfBandPaymentRecorded; absent.
recommended_change: See new defects for each gap. For this finding: add OutOfBandPaymentRecorded with duplicate suppression of the matching queued instruction; require that integrity or legally mandatory holds convert to a sponsor decision task and never silently expire; restore 'unilaterally' (or define execute vs instruct).

claim: Replicated versioned hold publications and a signed freshness beacon were added, but the mechanism cannot meet its own acceptance criterion, no replication-lag objective is declared or benchmarked, no numeric freshness bound exists, and two of the finding's ACs (stalled replica blocks only that cell; stale beacon yields HoldStateUnknown) are absent.
evidence: requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md CNV-ARC-003: 'dispatch SHALL compare, in the same local transaction, the cell's applied version with a signed registry version beacon no older than an approved freshness bound'; AC 'a hold published between authorization and dispatch ... the fencing check fails'. Finding rec: 'The replication lag objective (p99) SHALL be declared and benchmarked ... a stalled replica in cell A blocks only cell A's dispatch.'
recommended_change: Declare the p99 publication-to-applied lag and the maximum beacon age as numeric, basis-tagged values; state the residual exposure window (beacon age plus lag) explicitly and require legally mandatory holds (sanctions, revocation) to use a synchronous registry confirmation at dispatch; add ACs: stalled replica in cell A blocks only A; beacon older than bound yields HoldStateUnknown; benchmark reports achieved lag.

claim: The fence cannot satisfy its own acceptance criterion. A global OFAC or revocation hold is the case that matters most.
evidence: requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md CNV-ARC-003: 'dispatch SHALL compare, in the same local transaction, the cell's applied version with a signed registry version beacon no older than an approved freshness bound'; AC 'Given a hold published between authorization and dispatch, when dispatch runs, then the fencing check fails and nothing is transmitted.' recommended_change: State the residual exposure window as beacon age plus p99 publication lag, basis-tag both numbers, and require holds classified legally mandatory (sanctions, revocation, court order) to be confirmed by a synchronous registry check (fail closed on timeout) at the irreversible step. AC: a hold published 1 second after the latest beacon and before dispatch either blocks dispatch (mandatory class) or is reported in the dispatch record as inside the declared window (other classes).

claim: There is no single hold model, and the new time-bound rule collides with holds that must not expire. PLT-007 makes every platform-originated hold or fail-closed gate expire or convert within a default one business day, with the AC allowing silent expiry. But public-fact holds propagated by the registry (OFAC listing, revocation) are platform-originated and legally mandatory, GRT-005 says mandatory holds 'SHALL NOT auto-release', ARC-003's fail-closed gate stays closed for as long as the registry is down, and older holds (unmatched-debit hold 'until an authorized human classifies it'; state change without command event 'until reviewed') are unbounded. As written an OFAC hold, an integrity alarm or a registry outage can expire into release, or the clauses contradict each other.

PLT-007 SHALL apply only to discretionary platform safety holds; legally mandatory and public-fact holds SHALL never expire; integrity and fail-closed gates SHALL convert to a sponsor decision task and keep the platform path held until decided. ACs per type, including: OFAC hold older than one business day is still enforced; integrity hold at window end creates a decision task and does not release.

claim: The callback control can be defeated by a two-step attack and its source is undefined. recommended_change: A callback contact SHALL come only from (i) a record verified at least a sponsor-set period (default 30 days) before the change request or (ii) an independent public source recorded with retrieval date; any contact or signatory change inside that period disqualifies the contact. AC: contact change on day 0 and bank change on day 1 produces a callback to the pre-day-0 contact or a refusal; a contact with no qualifying record holds the release with DestinationEvidenceInsufficient.

ITGCs are effective, and the external auditor and board or audit committee have accepted the design'. requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md CNV-PLT-010: 'each release SHALL publish to each sponsor a notice listing changed control-relevant modules'.
recommended_change: A change to a gate module SHALL carry a materiality class; material changes require sponsor acceptance (and auditor notification) before activation for that sponsor, and until accepted the sponsor reverts to the three-distinct-person rule. AC: a material gate change released without a sponsor acceptance record leaves that sponsor on the three-person rule.
